metadata.research_goal: Create a backend-ready level-based teaching draft for indoor six-player volleyball that integrates Wave 1 technical, tactical, role, rules, and match-IQ drafts with official coaching resources and peer-reviewed performance and injury evidence. The draft defines beginner, intermediate, and advanced expectations, prerequisites, drills, avoid-until-ready gates, assessment signals, role-specific progressions, and transition rules for serving, passing/serve receive, setting, attacking, blocking, defense/digging, transition, match IQ, and volleyball strength and conditioning.

key_concepts.concept: Volleyball level is not defined by one flashy skill.
key_concepts.details: A player should move from beginner to intermediate or intermediate to advanced only when technical execution, tactical decision making, legal awareness, physical readiness, and match-transfer signals are all present for the target domain.

key_concepts.concept: Beginner volleyball should build broad game literacy before narrow role specialization.
key_concepts.details: New players need serve, pass, set, controlled attack, safe net play, rotation, communication, base defense, and three-contact intent before complex systems or role-only training.

key_concepts.concept: Intermediate players can specialize while retaining enough all-around skill to solve broken plays.
key_concepts.details: Role priority increases at this level, but every player still needs emergency second contact, controlled free ball, coverage, defensive communication, and basic serve-receive or transition responsibilities.

key_concepts.concept: Advanced development is driven by speed, deception, scouting, and pressure execution.
key_concepts.details: Advanced athletes must execute under live serve and attack speed, vary choices by opponent tendency, track phase-specific metrics, and manage load while preserving technical quality.

key_concepts.concept: Serve-receive and dig quality determine how much offense can be used.
key_concepts.details: Quicks, slides, pipe, setter attack, and combination plays belong behind positive pass or high-quality transition gates. Poor first contacts should trigger high, hittable, low-error options.

key_concepts.concept: Isolated drills are only a bridge to perception-action practice.
key_concepts.details: Wall passing, self-setting, and approach footwork can establish shapes, but assessments should use live or representative cues: server, setter release, block, hitter approach, score state, and rally consequence.

key_concepts.concept: Avoid-until-ready gates protect learning quality and athlete health.
key_concepts.details: Jump topspin serves, two-person receive, first-tempo combinations, swing blocking, commit blocking, back-row attacks, and emergency dive volume should be held until prerequisites are visible.

key_concepts.concept: Role progressions must respect legal row status and rule-set variants.
key_concepts.details: A setter, outside, opposite, middle, libero, DS, or serving specialist may have different tasks by rotation. Back-row attack-line rules, libero restrictions, and substitution rules must be stored with drills and tactical prompts.

key_concepts.concept: Blocking, floor defense, and transition attack should be taught as one chain.
key_concepts.details: The block shapes the dig, the dig shapes the set, the set shapes the attack, and coverage protects the next contact. Training that stops after a block jump or dig misses the rally value of the skill.

key_concepts.concept: Volleyball strength and conditioning should support skill repeatability rather than steal court quality.
key_concepts.details: Gym work should build jump, landing, shoulder, trunk, hip, ankle, and low-stance capacity while respecting court jump count, swing volume, serve volume, tournament density, and pain response.

technical_models.model: Serve progression moves from underhand or adapted-distance over-net success to standing float pressure, then jump float or jump topspin only when contact, target accuracy, shoulder tolerance, and landing control are stable.

level_summary.beginner: Serve over and in from legal or adapted distance; learn routine, contact point, large targets, and recovery into defense.
level_summary.intermediate: Use standing float as default pressure serve; serve zones 1, 5, 6, seams, short/deep targets, and score pressure sets.
level_summary.advanced: Select jump float, jump topspin, or tactical float by rotation, passer, score, and error threshold.

technical_models.model: Passing is an angle-control and reading skill. The passer reads server cues and ball flight, moves into a stable base, creates platform angle to target, and transitions to the next responsibility.

level_summary.beginner: Forearm pass to large target with early call and simple seam rule.
level_summary.intermediate: Receive float, topspin, short, and seam serves with midline and outside-body platforms in three- or four-person systems.
level_summary.advanced: Adjust starting depth and lane by server, use libero-priority seams, and connect pass grade to side-out plans.

technical_models.model: Setting combines early release, balanced arrival, legal contact, safe set location, and decision making based on pass quality, attacker availability, blocker position, and score context.

level_summary.beginner: High hittable front sets and emergency forearm sets.
level_summary.intermediate: Front/back options, basic tempo, out-of-system protocols, and second-setter calls.
level_summary.advanced: Jump setting, neutral release, setter attack, rotation distribution, and late blocker reads.

technical_models.model: Attacking is approach timing, takeoff mechanics, high contact, landing control, and shot selection against set quality, block shape, and defensive space.

level_summary.beginner: Approach rhythm, controlled swing or roll, line/cross broad zones, and safe landing.
level_summary.intermediate: High hands, tool, roll, tip, recycle, quick/slide/pipe introductions where legal and safe.
level_summary.advanced: Role-specific attack menus, combination timing, back-row attack, scouting, and pressure kill/error management.

technical_models.model: Blocking begins with pass-setter-hitter reading, then footwork matched to distance and tempo, balanced takeoff, hand penetration, legal net discipline, and safe landing into transition.

level_summary.beginner: Ready position, static press, one-step or shuffle block, and controlled landings.
level_summary.intermediate: Read block, crossover, double-block seam closure, and block-defense lane calls.
level_summary.advanced: Swing block, commit/read choices, scout-based hand plans, and role-specific jump-load monitoring.

technical_models.model: Defenders start from a system base, read pass, setter, set, block, hitter, and ball, then dig to a target that creates a realistic second contact and attack.

level_summary.beginner: Base position, low balanced posture, high-center dig, and simple tip responsibility.
level_summary.intermediate: Hard-driven, roll, tip, line, and cross reads with perimeter or rotational rules.
level_summary.advanced: Hybrid defense, hitter tendency reads, libero/DS leadership, and dig-to-attack efficiency.

technical_models.model: Transition connects block or dig to setter access, attacker release, set choice, attack selection, coverage, and reset. It should be trained as a sequence rather than a single skill.

level_summary.beginner: Dig or free ball to high target, call second ball, send controlled third contact, and cover.
level_summary.intermediate: Second-setter plan, dig-set-attack scoring, attacker release routes, and coverage layers.
level_summary.advanced: Fast transition from perfect digs, out-of-system counterattack choices, free-ball conversion, and phase-specific KPIs.

technical_models.model: Match IQ should tag rallies by serve pressure, side-out, transition, and extended rally so coaching actions match the actual problem.

level_summary.beginner: Know zones, rotation, front/back row, three contacts, call responsibility, and base positions.
level_summary.intermediate: Use side-out, breakpoint, pass grade, serve target, seam rule, and block-defense calls.
level_summary.advanced: Use rotation reports, conditional setter/hitter scouting, serve target expected value, and live adjustment loops.

technical_models.model: S&C readiness supports skill progressions through lower-body strength, landing mechanics, repeated jump ability, shoulder/scapular capacity, trunk control, hip/ankle mobility, low-stance tolerance, and recovery habits.

level_summary.beginner: Movement literacy, landing mechanics, basic strength, mobility, and pain-free participation.
level_summary.intermediate: Progressive strength, plyometrics, deceleration, shoulder care, and role-aware load tracking.
level_summary.advanced: Periodized power, repeated jump and overhead capacity, tournament recovery, and individualized load adjustments.

technical_models.model: Role specialization should increase by level while preserving all-around problem solving.

level_summary.beginner: All roles learn serve, pass, set, attack approach, defend, rotate, and communicate.
level_summary.intermediate: Setters, outsides, opposites, middles, liberos, DS, and serving specialists add role priorities and legal constraints.
level_summary.advanced: Roles train by rotation, matchup, opponent tendency, pressure routine, and load profile.

tactical_rules.rule: Choose serve risk by score, server skill, target value, and error history.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: Large target and high in-bounds rate come before ace seeking.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Standing float to weak passer, seam, short/deep zone, or overloaded attacker with tracked miss type.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Rotation-specific target and serve type chosen by expected disruption minus error cost.

tactical_rules.rule: Pass or dig quality determines tempo and option count.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: Use high hittable sets and controlled third contact from most first contacts.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Run middle, right-side, or faster pin only from positive passes and stable setter arrival.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Use pass-grade distribution to plan quick, slide, pipe, setter attack, and fallback high-ball choices.

tactical_rules.rule: Every serve-receive and defensive seam needs an owner before the ball is served or attacked.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: Use a fixed left-owns or right-owns rule and require a call.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Use libero-priority, short/deep split, or movement-based seam rules.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Adjust seam ownership by server type, passer strength, rotation, and outside-hitter attack value.

tactical_rules.rule: When set quality is uncertain, miss high, inside, and off the net rather than low, tight, outside the antenna, or over the net.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Hittable out-of-system outlet to trained attacker.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Target range varies by hitter approach lane, block matchup, and transition coverage.

tactical_rules.rule: Attack selection must fit set quality, contact point, block shape, and match risk.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: Controlled deep ball, broad line/cross, and roll shot before max power.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Add tool, high hands, tip, roll, recycle, and seam shots against live blockers.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Use scout-based shot charts and pressure-specific kill/error targets.

tactical_rules.rule: A block call must map to floor defenders, tip/roll ownership, and transition setter responsibility.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: Simple block/no-block lane plus high-center dig target.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Line or angle call with defender lanes and tip player.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Scout-based line/angle/seam hand plan with hybrid defense and transition route.

tactical_rules.rule: If the setter makes first contact or cannot take second contact cleanly, a preassigned second setter owns the ball loudly and early.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: Nearest player calls help and sends high ball.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Libero, right-back, or DS has trained second-contact target.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Second-setter plan varies by dig zone, role, libero legality, and attacker availability.

tactical_rules.rule: Named role never overrides current front-row/back-row status or libero rules.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: Players identify if they are front row or back row each rotation.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Back-row attack and libero setting constraints are attached to drills.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Rotation cards include legal attack, block, substitution, and libero choices.

tactical_rules.rule: A scout plan must translate into a small number of on-court actions.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: No opponent-specific scouting beyond obvious open space and weak contact.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: One scout cue per drill or match segment.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Serve target, block call, defensive lane, setter tendency, and fallback are rehearsed before competition.

tactical_rules.rule: Skill volume stops or regresses when movement quality, pain response, or decision accuracy degrades.
tactical_rules.beginner_application: Stop high-repetition overhead and jump drills when contact or landing falls apart.
tactical_rules.intermediate_application: Track jump serves, block jumps, swings, and hard-dig exposure.
tactical_rules.advanced_application: Adjust by role, tournament schedule, tendon response, shoulder symptoms, and match density.

physical_demands.demand: Volleyball requires repeated jumps for serving, attacking, blocking, jump setting, and transition.

level_progression.beginner: Learn two-foot landing, knee tracking, quiet trunk, and spacing before high volume.
level_progression.intermediate: Add approach jumps, block jumps, low-volume plyometrics, and landing under moderate randomness.
level_progression.advanced: Develop repeated jump ability, role-specific jump count tolerance, and power maintenance across match/tournament density.

physical_demands.demand: Serving, spiking, setting, and overhead defensive contacts load the shoulder, trunk, elbow, wrist, and fingers.

level_progression.beginner: Use controlled volume, clean mechanics, and broad targets.
level_progression.intermediate: Build shoulder/scapular endurance and track serve/swing/set counts.
level_progression.advanced: Separate high-speed swing volume, jump-serve load, setter hand volume, and shoulder symptom response.

physical_demands.demand: Serve receive, defense, and digging require low posture, lateral movement, hip mobility, reaction speed, and repeated short accelerations.

level_progression.beginner: Teach balanced ready posture without collapsing trunk or knees.
level_progression.intermediate: Add shuffle, drop-step, crossover, forward short-ball movement, and low-stance endurance.
level_progression.advanced: React to serve/hitter cues under fatigue while preserving pass and dig quality.

physical_demands.demand: Blocking and defensive release patterns require lateral acceleration, deceleration, spatial awareness, and safe landings near teammates and the center line.

level_progression.beginner: One-step and shuffle patterns with known targets.
level_progression.intermediate: Crossover and controlled swing-block movement with live setter reads.
level_progression.advanced: Unanticipated block movement, swing blocking, and release switches under scout constraints.

physical_demands.demand: Volleyball has intermittent high-intensity rallies with repeated technical efforts across practices, matches, and tournament days.

level_progression.beginner: Build general fitness and recovery habits while preserving skill quality.
level_progression.intermediate: Use conditioning through gamelike rallies and monitor high-intensity volume.
level_progression.advanced: Plan microcycles around match density, travel, jump load, and role-specific recovery.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Ankle sprains and contact landings are common around the net and during block/attack landings.
Repeated jumps, fast approaches, hard landings, and high block volume can overload the knee and patellar tendon.
Unanticipated block movement and poor landing mechanics can increase knee valgus, trunk control, and lower-limb risk.
Serving, jump serving, attacking, and high-volume overhead reps can overload the shoulder, especially when fatigue changes mechanics.
Repeated hitting, serving, emergency setting, and defensive extension can stress the low back.
Blocking, setting, and hard-driven digs expose fingers, thumbs, wrists, and hands to high-speed ball contact.
Digging, pursuit, and emergency floor skills can create shoulder, wrist, hip, and low-back load if taught as fatigue punishment.
Early role-only training and complex switching can reduce all-around problem solving and increase collision or confusion risk.

training_implications.implication: Every level should have entry criteria, teaching tasks, avoid-until-ready gates, and exit signals.
training_implications.application: The backend should not recommend advanced skills based only on age or roster role. It should check technical, tactical, physical, and match-transfer readiness.

training_implications.implication: Beginner training should adjust court size, net height, ball type, serve distance, and game numbers when needed to preserve rallies.
training_implications.application: The goal is more real contacts and decisions, not adult full-court failure repeated at low quality.

training_implications.implication: Drills should map to serve pressure, side-out, transition, or extended-rally outcomes.
training_implications.application: Serving practice tracks in-rate and opponent pass quality; receive practice tracks side-out; defense practice tracks dig-to-attack; transition practice tracks counterattack quality.

training_implications.implication: Role-specific plans should still include emergency second contact, controlled free ball, coverage, and communication.
training_implications.application: Specialization should not leave middles, pins, or defensive players unable to handle broken-play responsibilities.

training_implications.implication: Rules should be embedded in skill tasks, not taught only as trivia.
training_implications.application: Back-row attack drills include attack-line takeoff, libero second-ball drills include front-zone overhand-set restrictions, and blocking drills tag front-row eligibility.

training_implications.implication: The backend should store volume and quality together.
training_implications.application: Jump count without landing quality, serve count without shoulder quality, or dig count without playable target rate gives an incomplete recommendation.

training_implications.implication: S&C should start with movement capacity, progress to volleyball-specific power and deceleration, then integrate with court load.
training_implications.application: Avoid max plyometrics, fatigue conditioning, or heavy gym sessions immediately before high-speed timing practices.

training_implications.implication: Assessment should include brief decision explanations.
training_implications.application: Players should be able to state why they served a zone, passed a seam, set a high ball, chose a roll shot, or defended a lane.

training_implications.implication: Advanced teams need practice changing a plan after the opponent adapts.
training_implications.application: Use scout-team constraints and rotation-specific games where players must observe, compare, decide, communicate, test, and retain or revert.
